key_insight: Local neural operators can act as data-driven surrogates for complex spatiotemporal systems, allowing researchers to study stability and bifurcations without explicit equations or expensive brute-force simulation. By pairing them with equation-free analysis and Krylov subspace methods, the paper shows how to extract system-level behavior directly from data.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of analyzing large, complex dynamical systems when governing equations are unknown, incomplete, or too costly to simulate at scale. It enables stability and bifurcation analysis directly from data.
method: Train local neural operators to learn localized system dynamics from data.
Embed the learned model in an equation-free framework for coarse-grained analysis.
Use Krylov subspace techniques to compute system-level stability and bifurcation information efficiently.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a path from predictive modeling to interpretable system analysis, especially for scientific and engineering data. It reduces reliance on full simulations and opens the door to scalable analysis of complex physical systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data -> local neural operator -> equation-free analysis -> stability/bifurcation results

Block icons for neural operator, Krylov method, and system-level analysis
Before/after comparison of brute-force simulation versus data-driven surrogate analysis
paper_title: Enabling local neural operators to perform equation-free system-level analysis
paper_authors: Gianluca Fabiani, Hannes Vandecasteele, Somdatta Goswami, Constantinos Siettos, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis
